checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified that the ventral foot and defensive curling behavior are untestable due to the dorsal viewing angle and static pose. However, the Router was too lenient regarding the 'Dorsal surface protected by eight overlapping calcareous plates' checkpoint. While it noted the difficulty in counting, it marked the feature as present based on 'multiple distinct ridges.' Visually, the plate boundaries are poorly defined; they appear as shallow indentations or texture variations rather than distinct, overlapping calcareous valves with clear separation lines. The 'embedded' nature of the plates is ambiguous, looking more like a single segmented mass than individual plates set in a girdle. Additionally, the expert classifier ranked 'sea cucumber' higher than 'chiton,' suggesting the visual features (segmentation without clear plate definition) lean towards a different taxon, reinforcing that the specific chiton plate anatomy is not fully realized.
artifact_review: The Router identified a severity 2 texture anomaly in the background shell and a severity 1 structural collapse at the girdle-rock interface. I agree with these findings but elevate the severity of the boundary issue. The SAM mask reveals a disconnected lower-left segment, indicating the model struggled to define the organism's full extent, likely fusing it with the rock or failing to render the anterior tip coherently. The 'melting' at the bottom left is not just slight ambiguity; it represents a failure to render the distinct edge of the girdle against the substrate, violating the 'tough leathery girdle' physical property. The background shell's lack of micro-texture (severity 2) is also consistent with AI smoothing artifacts. The perceptual auditor found no noise/blur, confirming the issues are structural/semantic rather than compression-related.
alignment_reasoning: 7/9 checkpoints testable. Head/girdle/color checks passed. Plate definition is weak (boundaries indistinct, resembling sea cucumber segmentation more than chiton valves), supported by expert classifier ranking sea cucumber #1. Ventral/behavioral checks correctly marked N/A. Score penalized for ambiguous plate anatomy which is the defining feature of the class.
artifact_reasoning: Router found background softness (sev 2) and boundary melting (sev 1). Upgraded boundary issue severity due to SAM mask showing disconnected components and visual fusion of the girdle into the rock substrate. The lack of crisp plate boundaries contributes to a general structural softness. No global noise/blur detected.
